instruction: Independently review the candidate. Backward review receives only the private hierarchy; forward review receives only execution context. First decide whether the candidate action duplicates work already in context.existing_actions (every action tried or under review, with outcome and scores) or context.near_duplicates (closest matches, with similarity = word overlap and semantic = embedding similarity, both 0-1; duplicate=true means the engine already judges it the same action). Same source state, same resource versions and same effects is a duplicate even when titles, steps or wording differ: return duplicate_action and set duplicate_edge_id to that action's edge_id. Do not publish a rewording of something already tried; if that action failed, it is only distinct when the candidate states a concrete change that addresses the recorded failure. Otherwise compare inputs, resource versions, effects and state predicates: distinct means a genuinely different action; equivalent means it reaches an already-existing state (set equivalent_node_id). Uncertainty must remain unpublished (uncertain). An active outcome sourced from an accepted execution is an observed state and a permitted action source. Unexecuted milestones are not observations or equivalent completed states. For retirement, distinct means the retirement is justified, otherwise return uncertain or reject. For a backward milestone, near_duplicates lists similar existing milestones: return equivalent with equivalent_node_id when it restates one.
